sources.entry: Tunnelbear - Simple VPN service for secure browsing and location switching. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: TunnelBear
summary.one_liner: TunnelBear is a simple consumer VPN service that encrypts your internet connection, lets you pick a country, and changes your virtual location.
keywords: awesome mac proxy and vpn tools
use_cases: Unblocking websites and apps blocked by governments
Preventing ISP or network owners from seeing online activity
Playing games on distant servers without throttling
Unblocking sites on school or work networks
summary.what_it_does: TunnelBear encrypts the user's internet connection to keep online activity private on any network. Users open the app, select a country from a list of roughly 50 server locations, and switch the connection on. It assigns a new IP address to hide the user's real one from ad trackers and changes the virtual location to access region-restricted content. The page states it uses AES 256-bit encryption by default and says it does not monitor, log, or sell browsing activity. It also claims a global server network optimised for fast surfing and streaming.
notable: Country-select one-switch interface with a list of about 50 virtual locations
Publishes regular independent security audits of its apps (claimed as the only VPN doing so)
AES 256-bit encryption by default with no weaker option
Claimed no-logs policy for browsing activity
caveats: Page promotes a paid first-year offer at $39.99 USD with a 70% off fall sale; the free tier's limits are not described on this page
Only Mac, Windows, iOS, Android and Chrome are named; Linux is not mentioned
Security and no-logs claims are the vendor's own statements on the page
